items.stem: What was the Bombay Plan?
items.answer: A plan drawn up in 1944 by big industrialists, proposing state-led industrial and economic development with a joint role of state and private sector.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Planning Commission was not a constitutional body. There was a consensus that development could not be left to private actors and that the government should plan for it. Many people believed that development should not be measured only by economic growth but also by social justice. The Indian government's planning was influenced by the success of planning in the Soviet Union."
(i) Explain the term 'Bombay Plan', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: India adopted a mixed economy. (1)

items.answer: (i) The plan drawn up in 1944 by a group of big industrialists proposing a joint state-led industrial development. items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (the government wanted a body that would act as a think tank and promote cooperative federalism rather than central allocation.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Statement: The licence system was criticised.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It allowed the state to control what private industry produced and where, which encouraged corruption and inefficiency.
items.markingKey: (a) It allowed the state to control what private industry produced and where, which encouraged corruption and inefficiency.
options: It allowed the state to control what private industry produced and where, which encouraged corruption and inefficiency.
Planners believed that only the state could invest in basic and heavy industries needing huge capital.
The Second Plan concentrated resources on heavy industry and lacked an agrarian strategy.
The partition had badly affected agriculture and it was felt that agriculture needed urgent attention.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the early Five Year Plans and the Kerala model:
I. Industrialisation required foreign exchange, which India had to obtain by borrowing.
II. The Kerala model emphasised heavy industries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: It emphasised education, health, land reform and food distribution.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Assertion (A): India adopted a mixed economy.
Reason (R): The Bombay Plan was drawn up by the Communist Party.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: It was drawn up by a group of big industrialists in 1944.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on key controversies of planned development and answer the questions that follow.
"Many critics thought that the Second Plan lacked an agrarian strategy for the growth of agriculture. Critics argued that the public sector created vested interests and became inefficient. Some argued that the state's control created a licence raj that discouraged private enterprise."
(i) In India's planning, the 'commanding heights' of the economy were given to the: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'agriculture versus industry' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The public sector was given the commanding heights of the economy. (2)
items.answer: (i) public sector (ii) The controversy over whether planning should prioritise farming or industrialisation. (iii) Planners believed that only the state could invest in basic and heavy industries needing huge capital.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) public sector (ii) The controversy over whether planning should prioritise farming or industrialisation. (iii) Planners believed that only the state could invest in basic and heavy industries needing huge capital.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the early Five Year Plans and the Kerala model is NOT correct?
items.answer: The Kerala model emphasised heavy industries.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. It emphasised education, health, land reform and food distribution.
options: The government protected domestic industries by imposing tariffs on imports in the Second Plan.
The Kerala model emphasised heavy industries.

Industrialisation required foreign exchange, which India had to obtain by borrowing.

items.stem: In the study of key controversies of planned development, the term 'agriculture versus industry' refers to:
items.answer: The controversy over whether planning should prioritise farming or industrialisation
items.markingKey: (d) 'agriculture versus industry' means the controversy over whether planning should prioritise farming or industrialisation.
options: The plan for 1956–61 that stressed heavy industries, drafted under the leadership of P.C. Mahalanobis
The National Institution for Transforming India, which replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015
The development approach of Kerala focusing on education, health, land reform, effective food distribution and poverty alleviation
The controversy over whether planning should prioritise farming or industrialisation

items.stem:
Read the following statements about outcomes of planned development and the shift in economic policy:
I. After 1991, India moved away from state-led development towards liberalisation.
II. The Green Revolution benefited all regions equally.
III. NITI Aayog was set up in 1950.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (d) I is correct. II is incorrect: It benefited regions like Punjab, Haryana and western UP and rich farmers most. III is incorrect: The Planning Commission was set up in 1950; NITI Aayog replaced it in 2015.
options: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I only

items.stem:
Read the following extract on development models and the Planning Commission and answer the questions that follow.
"Many people believed that development should not be measured only by economic growth but also by social justice. There was a consensus that development could not be left to private actors and that the government should plan for it. The Indian government's planning was influenced by the success of planning in the Soviet Union."
(i) The Bombay Plan of 1944 was drawn up by: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Planning Commission' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Even industrialists supported planning in the 1940s. (2)
items.answer: (i) big industrialists (ii) The body set up in March 1950 by a simple resolution of the government, with the Prime Minister as chairperson, to make Five Year Plans. (iii) The Bombay Plan proposed state support for industrial development.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) big industrialists (ii) The body set up in March 1950 by a simple resolution of the government, with the Prime Minister as chairperson, to make Five Year Plans. (iii) The Bombay Plan proposed state support for industrial development.
